# Sirach 48 — Disagreement Log

**Chapter:** Sirach 48 | **Date:** 2026-03-17 | **Total Disagreements:** 20

---

## Disagreement 1 — 48:1, THE SIGNATURE LINE

**EMET:** "And Elijah arose like a fire, and his word burned like a torch."
**LOGOS:** "Then Elijah arose like fire, and his word burned like a torch."
**PNEUMA:** "Then Elijah arose like fire; his word blazed like a torch."
**Issue:** "Like a fire" (EMET) vs. "like fire" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) — Greek hōs pur = as fire. LOGOS/PNEUMA drop the article. PNEUMA changes "burned" to "blazed." All three are close to identical on this most famous line.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA follows LOGOS/PNEUMA: "like fire" (no article, stronger). "Burned" vs. "blazed" — SOPHIA retains "burned" for its gravity.

---

## Disagreement 2 — 48:2, "brought a famine upon them" vs. "brought famine upon them"

**EMET:** "He brought a famine upon them"
**LOGOS:** "He brought famine upon them"
**PNEUMA:** "He brought famine on them"
**Issue:** Greek elimou = of famine (genitive). EMET adds the article "a"; LOGOS/PNEUMA omit it. Minor.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA follows LOGOS: "He brought famine upon them."

---

## Disagreement 3 — 48:3, "three times brought down fire" vs. "three times called down fire"

**EMET:** "thus three times brought down fire"
**LOGOS:** "also three times called down fire"
**PNEUMA:** "three times called fire down from it"
**Issue:** Greek katēgagen = brought down. "Brought down" (EMET) is more literal; "called down" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) implies prayer/invocation.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "three times called down fire" — the invocation element is important to the story (1 Kings 18).

---

## Disagreement 4 — 48:4, "How glorified you were" vs. "How glorious you were"

**EMET:** "How glorified you were, Elijah, in your wondrous deeds!"
**LOGOS:** "How glorious you are, O Elijah, in your wondrous deeds!"
**PNEUMA:** "Elijah, how glorious you were in your marvelous deeds!"
**Issue:** Greek edoxasthēs = you were glorified (passive aorist). EMET "glorified" is more passive and literal; LOGOS "glorious" makes it a quality rather than something bestowed.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "How glorious you were, O Elijah" — "glorious" is more natural English, but the past tense honors the historical narrative.

---

## Disagreement 5 — 48:5, "from Hades" — placement

**EMET:** "raised a dead man from death and from Hades by the word of the Most High"
**LOGOS:** "raised a dead man from death, from Hades, by the word of the Most High"
**PNEUMA:** "raised a dead man back from death — from the very depths of Hades — by the word of the Most High"
**Issue:** PNEUMA adds "very depths" and "back" — no support in Greek. The comma placement (LOGOS) clarifies the two-part phrase.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA follows LOGOS with the clarifying comma.

---

## Disagreement 6 — 48:6, "men of honor from their beds"

**EMET:** "men of honor from their beds"
**LOGOS:** "honored men from their beds"
**PNEUMA:** "the honored from their beds"
**Issue:** Greek endoxous apo klinēs = glorious/honored ones from the bed. All three render essentially the same.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "men of honor from their beds" (EMET).

---

## Disagreement 7 — 48:8, "kings as avengers" vs. "kings to execute vengeance"

**EMET:** "who anointed kings as avengers"
**LOGOS:** "who anointed kings to execute vengeance"
**PNEUMA:** "you anointed kings to carry out vengeance"
**Issue:** Greek eis ekdikasin = for vengeance/as avengers. "As avengers" (EMET) is more nominal; "to execute vengeance" (LOGOS) is more verbal.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "anointed kings to execute vengeance" (LOGOS).

---

## Disagreement 8 — 48:8, "prophets as successors after him" — person shift

**EMET:** "prophets as successors after him"
**LOGOS:** "prophets as your successors"
**PNEUMA:** "a prophet to be your successor"
**Issue:** The passage shifts between 3rd and 2nd person in vv. 4–10 (direct address to Elijah). "After him" (EMET) shifts back to 3rd; "your" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) maintains 2nd person address.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "prophets as successors after you" — maintaining the 2nd person address.

---

## Disagreement 9 — 48:9, "whirlwind of fire" — the description

**EMET:** "taken up in a whirlwind of fire, in a chariot with horses of fire"
**LOGOS:** "taken up in a whirlwind of fire in a chariot with fiery horses"
**PNEUMA:** "swept up in a whirlwind of fire, in a chariot of horses of fire"
**Issue:** "Horses of fire" (EMET/PNEUMA) vs. "fiery horses" (LOGOS) — Greek hippōn purinōn = of fiery horses. The adjective "fiery" (LOGOS) vs. genitive "of fire" (EMET) is a legitimate choice.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA retains "horses of fire" — the genitive form preserves the strangeness of the imagery (2 Kings 2:11).

---

## Disagreement 10 — 48:10, end times vs. "for the times"

**EMET:** "appointed in the judgments to calm the wrath"
**LOGOS:** "appointed for the times to calm wrath"
**PNEUMA:** "appointed for the end times — to calm wrath"
**Issue:** Greek apokatastēsai = to restore; the Malachi allusion (4:5–6) is explicit. PNEUMA's "end times" is interpretive but the eschatological context is clear.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "appointed for the end times" — the Malachi allusion makes the eschatological sense clear and appropriate.

---

## Disagreement 11 — 48:11, "fall asleep in love" — what love?

**EMET:** "those who fall asleep in love"
**LOGOS:** "those who have fallen asleep in love"
**PNEUMA:** "those who have died in love"
**Issue:** Greek kekoimēmenoi en agapē = those who have fallen asleep in love. Whose love? Love of Elijah? Of God? Of one another? The ambiguity is real.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA retains "fallen asleep in love" — the ambiguity must stand; no gloss.

---

## Disagreement 12 — 48:11, "for we also shall surely live" vs. "we too shall surely live"

**EMET:** "for we also shall surely live"
**LOGOS:** "for we too shall surely live"
**PNEUMA:** "for we too shall live again"
**Issue:** Greek kai hēmeis zōēi zēsometha = and we also shall live by life. PNEUMA adds "again" implying resurrection. EMET/LOGOS are closer to literal.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA follows LOGOS: "for we too shall surely live."

---

## Disagreement 13 — 48:12, "wrapped in" vs. "enveloped in"

**EMET:** "Elijah was wrapped in the whirlwind"
**LOGOS:** "Elijah was enveloped in the whirlwind"
**PNEUMA:** "Elijah was swept up in the whirlwind"
**Issue:** Greek kaluphtheis = covered, wrapped. "Wrapped" (EMET) is most literal. "Enveloped" (LOGOS) is more evocative.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA retains "wrapped in the whirlwind" — the image of being wrapped (covered/enclosed) is more specific than "enveloped."

---

## Disagreement 14 — 48:13, "from wherever he had lain" vs. "even in death"

**EMET:** "from wherever he had lain, his body prophesied"
**LOGOS:** "even in death his body prophesied"
**PNEUMA:** "in death, his very body prophesied"
**Issue:** Greek apo koitēs autou = from his lying down/resting place. EMET preserves the spatial reference (2 Kings 13:21 — bones in the tomb); LOGOS/PNEUMA paraphrase.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "in death his body prophesied" (LOGOS) — clearer in English while preserving the miracle.

---

## Disagreement 15 — 48:15, "carried off as plunder" vs. "swept away as plunder"

**EMET:** "they were carried off as plunder from their land"
**LOGOS:** "they were carried off as plunder from their land"
**PNEUMA:** "they were swept away as plunder"
**Issue:** EMET/LOGOS agree. "Swept away" (PNEUMA) loses the "from their land" element.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA follows EMET/LOGOS: "carried off as plunder from their land."

---

## Disagreement 16 — 48:17, "bored through the rock with iron tools" vs. "tunneled through solid rock"

**EMET:** "he bored through the rock with iron tools"
**LOGOS:** "with iron tools he tunneled through solid rock"
**PNEUMA:** "he drove iron tools through solid rock"
**Issue:** Greek etrypasen en sidērō = he pierced/bored through with iron. "Bored through" (EMET) is most literal; "tunneled" (LOGOS) is more specific to the Hezekiah tunnel (2 Kings 20:20).
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "with iron tools he bored through the rock" — preserving the literal sense.

---

## Disagreement 17 — 48:18, "departed" vs. "withdrew"

**EMET:** "sent Rabshakeh and departed"
**LOGOS:** "sent Rabshakeh and withdrew"
**PNEUMA:** "sent Rabshakeh — then pulled back"
**Issue:** Greek apestrepsent = he turned away, withdrew. LOGOS "withdrew" is more precise military language.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "sent Rabshakeh and withdrew" (LOGOS).

---

## Disagreement 18 — 48:21, "messenger" vs. "angel"

**EMET:** "his messenger destroyed them"
**LOGOS:** "his angel annihilated them"
**PNEUMA:** "his angel wiped them out"
**Issue:** Greek angelos = messenger/angel. In the context of 2 Kings 19:35 (the angel of the LORD struck down 185,000), "angel" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) is more appropriate than the generic "messenger."
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "his angel destroyed them" — the divine messenger here is specifically an angelic being.

---

## Disagreement 19 — 48:22, "great prophet who was faithful in his vision" vs. "trustworthy in his vision"

**EMET:** "the great prophet who was faithful in his vision"
**LOGOS:** "great and trustworthy in his vision"
**PNEUMA:** "great and reliable in his visions"
**Issue:** Greek pistos en horamati = faithful/trustworthy in vision. "Faithful" (EMET) has more religious resonance; "trustworthy/reliable" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) is more functional.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "the great prophet, trustworthy in his vision" — "trustworthy" captures the prophetic credibility element.

---

## Disagreement 20 — 48:24, "a great spirit" vs. "by the power of the spirit"

**EMET:** "By a great spirit he saw the last things"
**LOGOS:** "By a great spirit he saw the end of things"
**PNEUMA:** "By the power of the spirit he saw the future"
**Issue:** Greek en pneumati megalō = in/by a great spirit. "Great spirit" is ambiguous — the divine Spirit or Isaiah's own greatness of spirit? PNEUMA interprets as "the power of the spirit." EMET/LOGOS retain the ambiguity.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA retains "By a great spirit" — the ambiguity is meaningful and should not be resolved.

---

*Total disagreements logged: 20*
